The '''Abhorchdienst''' (i.e. "Listening Bureau") was a German [[Cryptanalysis|code-breaking]] bureau which operated during the final years of the [[First World War]]. It was established in 1916 and was composed mainly of [[mathematicians]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Adams|first=Jefferson|title=Historical dictionary of German intelligence|year=2009|publisher=Scarecrow Press|pages=1}}</ref>  Other countries, such as [[France]] and [[Austria-Hungary]], had set up similar organisations at an earlier stage. Still, the military context did not necessitate the development of the German bureau until 1916.<ref name=Singh>{{cite book|last=Singh|first=Simon | authorlink= Simon Singh|title=[[The Code Book: The Secret History of Codes and Code-breaking]]|year=2010|publisher=HarperCollins}}</ref>
